clean_body: Add your name: No president is above the law = On day one as Attorney General, Todd Blanche’s Justice Department released a memo attempting to shield the President’s actions from future and retroactive investigations. It's illegal and unconstitutional. The memo argues that executive privilege can cover confidential presidential communications with private advisers. In practice, that could give Trump and his allies a new excuse to resist congressional subpoenas and obstruct future investigations. This is not an abstract legal debate. Congress has a constitutional duty to investigate corruption, expose abuses of power, and hold the executive branch accountable. A president cannot be allowed to create a blanket shield against scrutiny — especially one designed to reach backward and forward at the same time. As the top Democrat on the House Oversight Committee, I know exactly what is at stake when an administration tries to place itself beyond accountability. House Democrats will fight this in the courts. We will defend Congress’s oversight authority, the separation of powers, and the basic principle that the law applies to everyone. you for standing up for accountability. Robert Garcia = P.S. As the top Democrat on the House Oversight Committee, I’ll have subpoena power to finally hold the Trump Administration accountable — but only if we win back Congress this November. = = * Paid for by Robert Garcia for Congress Robert Garcia for Congress 65 Pine Ave #348 Long Beach, CA 90802 United States This email was sent to . **Last night, tens of thousands of Alaskans sent a clear message: We are ready for change.**

I’m so grateful for every Alaska voter who made their voice heard yesterday and cast their ballot for our movement. And I’m committed, over the next 76 days, to bringing as many Alaskans as we can into this fight with us.

From day one, this campaign has been about all Alaskans, regardless of where they live or who they vote for. That’s just as true today as ever.

Alongside our unique open primary system, Alaska also has ranked choice voting in the general. That means in November, voters will be able to rank up to four Senate candidates – myself, incumbent Republican Senator Dan Sullivan, and two others who will be determined in the coming days – in their order of preference.

**[This system rewards bipartisanship. Ted Stevens often said, to hell with politics, put Alaska first. Ranked choice voting encourages that mindset, and that’s exactly why I’m running. And I’m committed, over the next 76 days, to bringing as many Alaskans as we can into this fight with us. From day one, this campaign has been about all Alaskans, regardless of where they live or who they vote for. That’s just as true today as ever. Alongside our unique open primary system, Alaska also has ranked choice voting in the general. That means in November, voters will be able to rank up to four Senate candidates – myself, incumbent Republican Senator Dan Sullivan, and two others who will be determined in the coming days – in their order of preference. = = We are in a moral moment that needs real leadership. But instead, incumbent Senator Dan Sullivan has repeatedly taken votes that are injurious to Alaskans. He voted more than ten times for the Iran war, which is driving up our costs. He supported gutting healthcare, public radio, disaster relief, and veterans’ benefits. And he was revealed as the top recipient of corporate trawling industry donations in the Senate. He exemplifies what’s wrong in DC – a rigged system that puts corporate greed and self-serving politicians before the people. That’s why I’m running: Because Alaskans need an independent voice in the Senate who will stand up to anyone to put Alaska first, not DC special interests or billionaire donors. Last night’s result was a product of months of traveling to every corner of the state, and while I wouldn’t do anything differently, that means we’re heading into the general election with a huge cash-on-hand disadvantage. = = With all of you, we can win this November. Thank you! \- Mary | | | | | | | Resist Reclaim Rebuild is an organization committed to helping Democrats win up and down the ballot, nationwide. body:
170 Texas public schools have closed under Abbott.
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
Peter,
Here's a number that should keep every Texan up at night: **170.**
**That's how many public schools have closed in Texas over the last three years alone — under Greg Abbott's leadership.**
**170 schools.** Gone. Not because they weren't needed, not because communities didn't want them — but because Greg Abbott and his administration have failed our students, our teachers, and our families.
Every closed school represents kids who lost their classrooms. Teachers who lost their jobs. Communities that lost their future. **And Abbott's plan will be more of the same if reelected.**
Texas public schools simply cannot afford another four years of Greg Abbott.
That's why I'm running for governor — to fight for our schools, our students, and the future of this state. To fully fund public education, respect our teachers, and make sure every child in Texas has access to a quality education.
But I can't do it alone._I need you with me._
**[Will you chip in $5 or whatever you can today to help us defeat Greg Abbott and give Texas public schools the leadership they deserve?](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260820_3_schools.2FWnMq&refcode=em20260820-1886&amount=5&t=1&akid=1886%2E299639%2EIJJTQg)**

This is not a dry legal history. It is the story of a man born into crushing poverty in segregated Georgia. A man who was raised by a grandfather who worked him from dawn to dark and taught him that no one was coming to save him. A man who flirted with radical Left-wing politics as a young man and walked away from it. A man who studied to be a priest and ended up on the highest Court in the land. And a man who has spent thirty years insisting on one simple, radical idea: To celebrate the launch, I'm offering an opportunity to receive your copy while supporting this work: that **the Constitution -- not the personal views of nine justices -- is the highest law in this country.** For that, the Left has never forgiven him. I spent hours and hours interviewing Justice Thomas one-on-one for this book. It is wide-ranging. Very personal. Completely unguarded. He talks about the confirmation hearings. He talks about the years in the wilderness when even Conservatives kept their distance. He talks about what it cost to be right when everyone in the room is telling you that you are wrong. Team, Donald Trump has vowed to “nationalize” our elections by targeting mail-in voting... _And yet, he utilizes mail-in voting for his own gain._ | [ ](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137627744/641429507/1071238059?refcode=em-8.20.26-all-a-2&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzAvMS84OTkxNCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI3MDg1ZjMwOC1mZTljLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDBkM2ExMWZhMzAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=EsWtSQta73H62XiVGGlsskZWAujBTvn3R7pvBKEx5ho=) **Trump votes by mail again in his home state of Florida**
---
The White House is trying to spin this by calling Trump’s vote “a non-story.” But let’s lay out the facts:
When he spoke to millions last month, Trump called vote by mail _“inherently corrupt.”_
He’s repeatedly called on his Justice Department to _rig the system and force Federal control_ over who can and can’t receive a ballot in the mail – _despite the Constitution prohibiting the President from controlling our elections._
And in spite of all of this, Trump has voted by mail in Florida’s elections _twice this year._
It’s more than a “non-story,” team. This is about an administration who will rig the game in their favor at our expense – whether it’s weaponizing our federal government or having Trump’s allies run to be Secretaries of State across the country.

| NOTE: The following Op-Ed is being distributed for Seth Aitken for Bristol County District Attorney
FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE CONTACT: Vincent Errichetti 617 922 1824
ICE Was There to Protect Taunton. No One Let Them
If Massachusetts agencies had simply notified ICE before releasing Heriton Da Silva Aredes after any of his prior arrests, he would have been in federal custody instead of behind the wheel on Court Street; cooperation that costs nothing would have prevented the crosswalk killing.
Here is the story.
Heriton DaSilva Aredes is a Brazilian national with a substantial record of criminal convictions who previously entered into the United States illegally and was removed by Immigration in 2008.
From 2023, when he was arrested for driving without a license, until recently, Heriton DaSilva Aredes was apparently living in Taunton.
On the morning of November 20, 2024, Mr. Aredes was driving a borrowed motor vehicle, accelerated in front of a school bus on Court Street by the Taunton Green and killed a pedestrian in a cross walk. He was charged with Motor Vehicle Homicide in August 2025 and scheduled to be arraigned in Taunton District Court in November 2025.
Mr. Aredes did not show up for his arraignment. He was arrested on a default warrant more than a month later and, following that arraignment, was held on $2,500 cash bail. For the next seven+ months, unable to make bail, Mr. Aredes was held at the Bristol County House of Correction while his case progressed in the Taunton District Court. Mr. Aredes was transported to court in custody on July 23, 2026 and two days later, somehow posted bail and was released from the House of Correction. Despite a federal immigration detainer having been filed with the Bristol County Sheriff, the Sheriff elected not to notify immigration officials that Mr. Aredes had posted bail and released him back into society.
He was taken into custody by ICE on August 6, 2026.
Recently, Bristol County Sheriff Paul Heorux has claimed that Massachusetts law prevents his office from complying with Immigration detainers. While politically convenient, this is untrue. The Sheriff cites the 2017 court case of Lunn v. Commonwealth as cover for his decision to ignore ICE. The Lunn case stands for the proposition that law enforcement, including court officers, are prohibited from holding an individual solely on the basis of a federal civil immigration detainer.
An immigration detainer requests two things from any law enforcement agency holding someone in custody: 1) 48 hours of additional detention to give immigration officials time to arrive and take the person into custody or 2) advance notice before a person is scheduled to be released. While the Lunn case prohibits compliance with the first request - extended detention, nothing prohibits a sheriff's department from giving courtesy notice to ICE before an alien subject to removal is released back into the public.
The Bristol Sheriff's Office could have easily and lawfully given Immigration officials notice that Mr. Aredes was arranging to make bail. Instead, the Sheriff chose to take a progressive political stand by ignoring the immigration detainer and putting the public at risk. Mr. Aredes' criminal record was available to the Sheriff. The Sheriff knew Mr. Aredes had killed someone with a car and he knew that when given the opportunity, Mr. Aredes would very likely disappear and not show up to court. Most importantly, the Sheriff would have known that Mr. Aredes had been previously removed from the United States and had re-entered, a felony under federal law.
Perhaps, most important of all, the Sheriff was very likely aware that in the years preceding Mr. Aredes' motor vehicle homicide charge, he had been arrested several times by different Massachusetts law enforcement agencies and each time, either in defiance or ignorance of an immigration detainer, was released before ICE could respond. Had any of those agencies honored the detainer, if only to give ICE sufficient notice of Mr. Aredes' imminent release, the man who Mr. Aredes killed in that Taunton crosswalk might still be alive.
Here, knowing all that - fully aware of the harm that could have previously been avoided with a modicum of cooperation and communication - the Bristol County sheriff still followed through on his promise to ignore ICE efforts and released Heriton DaSilva Aredes to an unsuspecting public.
Whether motivated by politics or arrogance, the Sheriff's choice only served to make Bristol County less safe and serves as a startling example of what can happen when progressive politicians care more about indulging their hatred of conservative ideals than they care about their sworn duty to protect the innocent.

## Trump Declares 'Economic D-Day' on Iran
President Trump announced what he calls "[Economic D-Day](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkD3O3SAURFeDO57g4t-CIg3dlzaldR9c2yQYLMB-8u4jR4qygNQzOpozP77mL_TBx_U77qTrkuZInxKoVsoz2RTT7q1zeKfoM8ZyHpQpzCCg52LkIGe01V80t9g4vRABqYa0HMZBib6fpmbTyyitmhS2IyAuqh3UW3aiF6rr7ETWNl4_PDGClEK0Xf9qQcDoeiftG5W1xFpBzteUXz-Tj3WjJdzpovyyaW-C3mo9ClPfGBgGJt5HKvWJGJgHzMCIkYGREwNzFv4YMjA1n_vBMcZ0RkuF_7Xljju8Oa7oY6n80eZ7KpXbfJbNx_VfMx2UsfoUOV2UecVfFBmYJmt3fHwIvvQDa8W6ow9_ttb_vPjS8DsAAP__IWSSmw)" against Iran, vowing economic warfare "on an unprecedented scale" after a 60-day negotiating window closed Monday with no deal. He warned any country that offers Iran a financial "lifeline" will face "tremendous" consequences of its own, naming oil smuggling, cash transfers, and front companies. _"It all needs to stop NOW. You know who you are,"_ he wrote on Truth Social. [See the post here](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LFu6yAUxvGngS0RHGOwB4YrXXlLp0odrWM4jqkwWEAS5e0r9xW6fp_0G_5ft_mGIYZ0_8CdbFvznOhVI7VGZSaXU96D8x7fOYWCqT4OKhRnEKAvYriAnNG18KRZIfd2JQLqOFlpBtMJrceRb9aPS-ccakNukcPoYYVFo1Rm6dQyrD0P9vTEAFIKoXp9VSBg8NpLt2DnHDElyIeWy_U7h9Q2WuM7P6lcXd55tFtrR2XdPwYTg6mVR9tqdgHj-Z-jEoUw_s8Jo_8sj_1gMB25tspgktJIULoXozDa9EpLXqw_XiHGULVhStx3DL8Ub38s9LTwEwAA__9Ms3n0). Tehran is said to be looking for workarounds. Russia is reportedly [shipping ammunition](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOtCAUhZ9GOwwgohYUfzPd_O2W5g5cxrtBMIDjzttv3GSfYNtzkpPzfR_35Q4UKD7_w4am-rREPEvAWjEvaFNMG1nn4J0iZYjl2DFjWCSXmvGJSbGArfTCRUHrjEeU2LdoxDiNPdd6ntvVwOAGK6XGYXrAbFEpofuh57PQvRgnaMlce3ySQnCuBt0pyeXktBP2Ab212CiOjmrK3WeiWFf04Z1emDubtjaYtda9NP2_Rt4aeTvPs_Pp6-K4-itJObhG3i4CVmEvzFOEaAkCC-QxUESWj1IIIoO8FVbzse0Mi4UAFQuz-SgrxSf7VcJOyB4yttm4_aQQqOixUfy5AYWfW_WPNl9GfgcAAP__WZ6OHQ), drone parts, and explosives to Iran across the Caspian Sea, and Iran's central bank chief says the country will soon join a BRICS-backed development bank. Iranian inflation hit 62% in February, and food prices have more than doubled in a year. The UAE, Iran's [largest import source](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkD1uhDAUhE9jOqPHgzVQuEhDt2lTImM_Fkf-QcastTl9xOYI6UYa6dN883Wf78o6Gx6fypPMa5wDlcNRzpRm0jFEb7Ux6hWDTSoc506J3IyAgsPAsZmVzvZJc6cqI1cipLYi2fRD34IQ41ht8raguUEvmnEdNSzdQIQGqFX9ggsgVVZePBiwaQC6m6g7BByMMI1eVKs1sQ7I2BxT_R1tyBut7hWflGodfeXklvN-sPaD4cRwKqXUOiz6KhlOF5rhBMM7M5wuD_6n9uIlpmTp4DmdfueHCjrbGHhRiW8x-fOHn4p4vWXvqiTNXqxz9hA96-DhlXXvBfmfxz0l_gYAAP__kFGDcg), halted all trade on Wednesday after what it said were two Iranian missiles fired at the country.
## North Korea Fires 10 Ballistic Missiles
North Korea fired about 10 short-range [ballistic missiles](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykUD2OtDAUOw10QUngC6FI8TXTzbZbovDyGN5MflASBs3tV-wVtrIly5bt7_t8t-QpPr5sQFPXNEc8i8daMc8IKaZA4Jz9pEjZxnLsmNHPkkvFuGZSzBYqvXEebOvMiiixb9GIUY89V2qa2s30UmuxLCAmqwYYuVDTqt0KY697J6elJXPlcS2F4Hz4p7pBcqmdcgIW2wNgM3B0VFPunoli3XD1n_TG3EEKrTdbrXtp-v-NvDXydp5nB0u5dlx6I28XvSDlurFXymhZoFLII_P2iLCxmo-wsxcF9kzxwY7I4gEebWYn2j3Fy95m4_aTvKeixmbgj2DJ_zaofzzubeRPAAAA___fc4WN) Thursday, a day after President Trump said he expects to meet Kim Jong Un later this year. The launches came in the final days of U.S.-South Korean military exercises. Trump said he [ordered the exercises cut short](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0D2u2zAQBODTUB0NainTVMEijTqnTSkw5MrahD8Cubbj2wd6V3j1ADP45td9vXtKVB4_fUbHW10LvntCZmwrhlpqphCj_9RCzZf-PLBhWkGBkcpKGFcfmF64Tn6IbkME1AO68WZvWhkzz8Pu1KzQbgauANs8WfBe2TCbzZsxajvNA7mzT1kYR6Wmq7lMoMBGE8fw2-sQUEwKI3Ftlz-VCu-4pU99YbuEmofkduajC_1DwCJg4R13SunMBCx7zXiSBCw-ZirUuXmmWgQsRmltr1pye-ZD9vrkXf6tDb3MlIh9-0j8hy1Qxy5PvoBlaC4eb0qJurmJST2yp6-tgb9538vB_wAAAP__EI2GYQ) after asking South Korea's president to "give us a little hand" with Iran and being told, "No thanks." The two sides do not agree on the size of Pyongyang's arsenal. South Korea's defense minister told lawmakers the North is believed to hold [80 to 120](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGOnTAUBNCvMZ2fzIXl8QoXaeg2bUp0sYfFibGRrwHt30ebYn8g7Yw0Gp1f7_M7hxjSx0_eYeua54RbImpFmeFyyntw3vNnTqFwkvNAQZzJ0KDNqKmd2dVwYe658XYFCF0D2z7HZ2eG4fVqNtuavsero5EWt3APQ0_jfTe-OXIdRm6C_dozI7WtMf3b8OjJ0OgH37qFO-egegMfai6P3zmkumGNn_lCebi8N9FutR6iuh-KJkXTfd-PgrOiyFevaFpOCQkiiiZGyXKwg_ZYkQSKJsln3fSfXMAaUsPOFaJTLt_pxqLPQ7dkdDpdBBd9c9nAXvTKRfOSL-hazv0Q_W1jFE1Nsf64Q4xBhqfqzcfOIf67Xf9T-7L0NwAA___-Qpbu) nuclear warheads, well above the 57 that Trump cited a day earlier.

South Korean officials said the higher range comes from private researchers and said Seoul will keep relying on the U.S. nuclear umbrella rather than build its own arsenal.
